mu_name_from: Lorencia's object slot 30, from the client's own table. WorldObjectCatalog.cs records world 1 as a set of named runs rather than a flat list - Tree at 0, Grass at 20, Stone at 30 - so Stone01.bmd is object type 30 and there is no friendlier name than what the run is called.
why_this_one: The first world object, chosen to be the smallest thing that is honestly a world object rather than an item in a field. It has the two properties that separate scenery from everything built so far and no others: more than one sheet on one model, and one of those sheets a cut-out. A fence would have had neither, a house four sheets and five meshes of them.
sheet_from: Data/Object1/ston01.OZJ (128x128) and ston02.OZT (32x32), both from MuMain. The .bmd names ston01.jpg and ston02.tga, and the extension is the format rather than a different file: OZJ is MU's JPEG and OZT its TGA, so a sheet with an alpha channel is always an .OZT. Object1 holds a ston02.OZJ and a ston02.OZT that are different pictures, so neither may hold the bare name; this one wears the .tga, which is what the .bmd asks for. See tests/sheets.py.
sheet_note: remaster_one's copies are 512x512 and 128x128 - 4x both, where every item sheet so far was 2x. A different multiplier, the same tree, and MuMain's is the art.
cutout_from: ston02.OZT carries a real alpha channel that cuts away 55% of its square, which is a grass tuft drawn on a card. Declared rather than detected: the pipeline can also sniff it off the sheet, and the record of the last time that was trusted is in the Plate helm's feather.
material_note: Assigned per sheet rather than per island, which is what the tiled path made possible and what scenery wanted all along: ston01 is the rock face and ston02 is a grass tuft, and no island had to be looked at to know either. The island list below is kept as the record - it is also the evidence that the assignment is right, because the thirteen islands whose mu_uv is the whole square total exactly the twenty-six triangles the .bmd reports for ston02.
tiling_note: Island 0's UVs run from -0.44 to 1.33, well outside the square. That is not a fault, it is the point: ston01 is a tiling rock face and the boulder wraps it round itself more than once. It is also the evidence the world profile's wrap pad was written for - the texel past the right edge of that sheet really is the texel at the left edge.
open_question: The pad is one setting for the whole asset, and tiling is a property of a sheet. ston01 tiles and wants wrap; ston02 is a sprite and does not. It happens not to matter here because ston02's border is entirely cut away, so there is nothing at its edges to feed anywhere - but the next world object with an opaque sprite on it will want the pad to be per-sheet.
was_blocked: Baked, this came out with the boulder holding 18.2% of the map and its thirteen grass cards taking 58.6%, from two causes: identical islands each got their own region, and island 0 spans 2.37 sheets of UV because ston01 tiles. Neither is a size that can be tuned. It is what the world profile's tiled path was written for; see tiled_materials in export_gltf.

islands.note: the boulder itself - eighty of its hundred and forty triangles, and the island whose UVs run outside the square because ston01 tiles across it.
